mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for two consecutive months signals a prolonged easing cycle, which reduces risk-free rates and increases present value of corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for two consecutive months ending at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 3% signals strengthening domestic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 3% at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation expectations, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% for three consecutive months ending at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based weakening in supply and demand, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -2% MoM and HOUST < -2% MoM at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall by more than 2% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75 percentage points within a quarter signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.75% within the previous quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after such a rate hike episode (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS growth) both rising above 2% month-over-month indicates robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings and equity prices, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2% MoM and RSAFS > 2% MoM at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed 2% MoM growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8.0% for two consecutive months ending at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) with no corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a supply-side shock, which raises inflation and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% MoM and HOUST < -1% MoM and UNRATE change ≈ 0% at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO and HOUST fall but UNRATE is stable (t-test p > 0.05).
